clue.text: Stand in place on island in river

indicators.note: the river word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: the place piece is set down next to the island, which comes second

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take up a position on an island in the middle of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a substitute for someone, standing in for them.

clue.text: Like English chaps in financial difficulty, in shame

indicators.note: the first three pieces are placed inside the money-trouble word

parts.note: being in debt is financial difficulty
as means like
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Englishmen sinking into money trouble feel humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Debasement is a lowering in dignity or esteem, a degradation akin to disgrace.

clue.text: Slip in the bedroom

parts.note: suggests a fall or a nightdress, but a slip is also a cover for a pillow

explanation.surface: Someone trips over, or wears an undergarment, in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow slip is another name for the fabric cover on a bed pillow.

clue.text: Dodgy operator catching river fish

indicators.note: the dodgy dealer grabs the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a tout resells tickets at inflated prices, a shady trader

explanation.surface: A shady character lands a fish from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater game fish.

clue.text: The fops glide around — can't go any faster

indicators.note: the fops moving around suggests these letters being moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Dandies glide about, unable to pick up any more pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics nothing can exceed this ultimate cosmic speed limit, around 300,000 km per second.

clue.text: Minister losing head meeting American — one on perilous journey

indicators.note: the minister word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a vicar is a minister of the church
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A clergyman teams up with an American, cast as a traveller on a dangerous trip.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell, the classic hazardous flight.

clue.text: Bat, maybe, showing hesitation to pursue insect

indicators.note: the hesitation follows behind the insect

parts.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A dithering creature chases a bug, as a bat might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' suggests the flying mammal chasing insects; it is a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman in cricket is called a bat, one kind of player of the game.

clue.text: Start making bread?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to begin, as cameras ... when filming starts
a bread ... is a small loaf

explanation.surface: Is it time to begin baking?
explanation.definitionFit: Roll means to set going, as in let's roll, and is also a small individual loaf.

clue.text: Broadcast from name-dropping Channel 4 presenter

indicators.note: the name letter is dropped down to a lower place in the presenter's surname

parts.note: Jon Snow presented Channel 4 News in the UK for decades

explanation.surface: A TV newsreader is accused of name-dropping on air.
explanation.walkthrough: N moves from second place to the end of SNOW; down clues read top to bottom, so it drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed that has been broadcast has been scattered, so sown.

clue.text: Place for parliamentary beast — slob's a clue

parts.note: the clue word is what you get when the first four letters of the place are turned over, so the place serves as a clue to it

explanation.surface: A lazy layabout is offered as a hint to a place linked with a notorious parliamentarian.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis Skinner, long-serving Labour MP for this Derbyshire seat, was nicknamed its Beast. Split it as BOLS OVER: BOLS turned over gives the clue word, so the place is a clue for slob.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolsover is the constituency of the MP known as the Beast, so it is that beast's home ground.

clue.text: Big cloud making one under the weather in part of London

indicators.note: the poorly word sits within the London district

parts.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London
being under the weather means feeling unwell or sick

explanation.surface: A huge cloud makes someone in a London district feel poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making one' is only a link here: the sick piece goes inside BOW, an East End district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a large surging mass, as of smoke or cloud.

clue.text: Evil vicar's abused scripture — minister may hear from me

indicators.note: the letters are mistreated and knocked out of order

parts.note: NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A wicked clergyman misuses the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges EVILVICARS into CIVILSERVA; 'minister' is a government minister, not the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Government ministers are briefed and advised by officials of the permanent administration.

clue.text: Sweet little boy seen taking the lead

indicators.note: the seen word goes in front, leading the boy's name

parts.note: something seen has been spotted
Dick is a pet form of the boy's name Richard

explanation.surface: A cute little lad is noticed walking in front.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding with currants; 'Sweet' is a British word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This currant pudding is a classic British dessert, and a dessert course is called a sweet.

clue.text: Female, exhausted, see, temptress first off to have emotional experience

parts.note: all in means worn out
lo means look or see

indicators.note: the temptress's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Eve tempted Adam with the apple

explanation.surface: A worn-out woman watches a seductress leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming smitten with someone is a powerful romantic experience.

clue.text: Good source of energy alternative — fellow briefly giving its description?

indicators.note: take the opening letter of the energy word

parts.note: other means alternative
a fellow is a male; briefly cuts off the final letter

explanation.surface: A clue describing a promising form of renewable power.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the clue: heat from the earth is a good alternative energy source, and this word describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Geothermal describes heat drawn from inside the earth, an alternative power source.

clue.text: Drink tea when meeting doctor

indicators.note: the tea joins up with the doctor, coming after it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
cha (char) is informal British for tea

explanation.surface: Someone takes tea while seeing their doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a coffee drink, often flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: Hate in province with rabble rising in the grip of a troublemaker

indicators.note: the reversed pieces are held inside the outer pair

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading these letters backwards

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
a mob is a rabble

explanation.surface: Loathing in a region where a mob rises up, gripped by an agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NIMOB into BOMIN, which goes between A and ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest intensely.

clue.text: Ethical business — or one getting some taken for a ride?

definitions.meaning: commerce that pays producers decently, a recognised ethical label

definitions.text: one getting some taken for a ride?
definitions.meaning: business done at a funfair, where customers pay to go on rides; being taken for a ride also means being cheated

explanation.surface: Is principled commerce really just another way of conning people?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: commerce at a fairground, whose customers are literally taken on rides, playing on 'taken for a ride' as cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair trade is commerce guaranteeing growers a fair price, hence ethical; read as fairground commerce it sells rides.

clue.text: Heretic Tories naughtily invading student organisation

indicators.note: the shuffled party word forces its way inside the student body

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

indicators.note: behaving naughtily, the letters of Tories misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: Mischievous Conservatives storm a students' union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' is the anagram signal; NUS is the UK's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestorius was a 5th-century archbishop of Constantinople condemned for heresy about Christ's nature.

clue.text: Roof worker returning with new enthusiasm?

indicators.note: coming back, so the worker's title is read backwards

parts.note: a tiler lays tiles on roofs

explanation.surface: A roofer comes back to work fired with fresh zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fired up again has been rekindled, a figurative way of describing renewed enthusiasm.

clue.text: What Jacob wrenched from Esau, being the cannier, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, but here it signals an elaborate rearrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A speaker muses that Jacob, being the craftier brother, seized something from Esau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' looks like a throwaway aside, but I is fodder and 'fancy' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob tricked his elder brother out of his birthright and their father's blessing, his rightful legacy.

clue.text: Mark's hat worn by daughter

indicators.note: the hat goes on and around the daughter letter

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A girl puts on a hat belonging to Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy accent sign placed over letters such as the Spanish ñ.

clue.text: Report of competent shepherd

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word sounding like the capable one

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: A news item about a skilled herdsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel, Adam's second son, was a keeper of sheep.

clue.text: Upcoming strike creates difficulty

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: tonk is informal British for hit hard

explanation.surface: A planned walkout causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a tangled problem, a difficulty hard to unravel.

clue.text: Small message prohibiting certain headgear

parts.note: a ban is a message forbidding something
a tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish woollen cap

explanation.surface: A notice forbids wearing a particular kind of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantam describes a miniature breed of chicken, so it is used to mean tiny or diminutive.

clue.text: Cleaner has everyone locked in entertainment hall

indicators.note: the everybody word is shut up inside the sweeping tool

parts.note: a broom is a cleaning tool
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A cleaner has shut everyone inside a hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall used for dances and other entertainments.

clue.text: The second drink ending in disaster

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee drink

indicators.note: take the final letter of the disaster word

explanation.surface: A second round of drinks ends in calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Of two things mentioned, the latter is the one named second.

clue.text: This place, with the others around it, is heavenly

indicators.note: the others surround the place word, enclosing it

parts.note: et al. is Latin shorthand for and the others
this place is here

explanation.surface: A spot surrounded by companions is described as divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means celestial or otherworldly, delicate as the upper air of the heavens.
